newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Comalco NZ slides steeply to loss in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Comalco NZ slides steeply to loss in 1996.

text.p: Comalco New Zealand Ltd, controlled by Comalco Ltd, slumped to an after-tax loss of NZ$13.5 million in calendar 1996 from a 1995 profit of $106.9 million.
The profit fall largely reflected weaker primary aluminum prices, the LME price averaging US$1,535/tonne compared with $1,832 in 1995, the company said.
Operating costs were higher, reflecting complexities associated with commissioning the NZ$464 million upgrade of the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in the South Island and higher power prices.
Comalco said the strength of the New Zealand dollar had a substantive negative impact although this was offset by the favourable impact on US dollar borrowings.
Production capacity increased to 313,000 tonnes by year end from 270,000 tonnes.
Shareholders' equity was $644.7 million at December 31 against $658 million a year earlier and net debt to net debt plus equity increased from 14.7 percent to 29.9 percent over the year.
Comalco's share of exports from the Tiwai Point smelter increased to 198,595 tonnes from 187,550 tonnes and there was a "good lift" in domestic sales.
Comalco said world aluminium production grew in 1996 but remained below capacity.
Comalco said that the smelter upgrade was showing clear signs of improvement towards achieving its objectives.
